venue.name: Coast Salish Journey
venue.description: Coast Salish Journey is a group of Coast Salish artists and artisans founded by master wood carver Herb Rice, whose studio is at Whippletree Junction on the Trans-Canada Highway south of Duncan. The site is a gallery of commissioned work: totem poles, masks, drums, doors, panels, plaques and talking sticks. The one bookable offering it describes is a two day Introduction to Woodcarving workshop, and the workshop page says all classes are cancelled until further notice. Nothing on the site is written for a school class or a daycare group, and no visitor hours, prices or facilities are published.
venue.address: #41 - 1540 Cowichan Bay Road, Cowichan Bay, BC V0R 1N1
venue.seasonal_notes: All classes canceled until further notice. Please keep in touch, Thank You.

programs.name: Introduction to Woodcarving workshop
programs.description: A two day workshop with Herb Rice at Whippletree Junction, south of Duncan. Participants are introduced to knife making and care, to the different woods used, and to basic North West Coast technique and design, and each person carves a Killer Whale plaque using traditional bent knives and straight knives. Wood, designs, knives and all finishing materials are provided, some of the finishing has to be done at home, and lunch is at a local cafe at extra cost. The page carries a notice that all classes are cancelled until further notice, and gives no price, no dates, no age range and no group size.
programs.our_note: Nothing on this site is set up for a class or a daycare group. The one thing published is a two day carving workshop for individuals, using bent and straight knives, with no age guidance at all. The page also says classes are cancelled until further notice, so email before you plan anything around it.
programs.practical_summary: There is no visitor information on the site, so washrooms, lunch space, parking, accessibility and how long a session runs are all unknown. Email is the only way in, and the workshop is currently not running.
programs.extra_fees_note: LUNCH will be available at local cafe, added cost. Knives will be available for purchase during the class.
programs.evidence: This two day workshop is specifically for those who have been interested in carving

gaps: No hero photograph. The only photo on the home page is a portrait of the artist credited to a newspaper, which is a headshot and a third party credit, so it was not used. The workshop pictures page has small snapshots only, one of which is recorded here.

Nothing is bookable by a school or a daycare group. The home page says Herb Rice has taught in public schools, private schools and universities, but that is biography and not an offering the site sells or describes. The only bookable thing published is the individual two day carving workshop.
The workshop is not running. The page says all classes are cancelled until further notice and gives no restart date.
No price, no ages, no group size, no dates and no session times for the workshop.
No visitor hours, washrooms, lunch space, parking, accessibility or wet weather information anywhere on the site.
The site is years out of date. The workshop registration link still carries a September 2018 subject line, and the artists page links to a web directory that no longer serves a real site.
The contact addresses do not agree with themselves. Several links show an @coastsalishjourney.com address but point at a telus.net or yahoo.ca mailbox underneath. Recorded in conflicts.
The address recorded is the mailing address from the artists page. The map on the location page pins Whippletree Junction, which is what the coordinates here come from.
months unknown: the site never says when workshops run.
